## Preliminaries {#preliminaries}

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,

```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)  # for data wrangling and visualization
library(psych)      # for describe() and scoreItems()
library(janitor)    # for frequency and contingency tables
library(broom)      # for tidy t-test output
library(papaja)     # for APA style output
library(lsr)        # for cohensD()
library(BrailleR)   # for accessibility
GoBlind()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 16))
```

## Data

```{r}
df <- read_csv('data/tworek2016_study2.csv') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(diff, excluded) %>% 
  filter(excluded == 0)
glimpse(df)
```

```{r}
describe(df) %>%
  knitr::kable() 
```

## Check Assumptions

### Normality

```{r}
df %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = diff)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 9, color = "black", fill = "lightblue") +
    labs(x = "Inherence Bias", y = "Frequency") +
    theme_classic()
```


```{r}
shapiro.test(df$diff)
```

## One-Sample t-Test

```{r}
res_t <- t.test(df$diff,
                mu = 0, 
                alternative = "two.sided")
res_t
```

```{r}
res_apa <- res_t %>%
   apa_print()
res_apa$full_result
```

`r res_apa$full_result`

### Effect Size (Cohen's d)

```{r}
d <- cohensD(df$diff, mu = 0)
d
```

## Write up the results

> A one-sample t-test was performed to compare the mean relative preference of inherent over extrinsic explanation to the baseline of 0. The mean preference was significantly above the baseline, `r res_apa$full_result`, with a small effect size, d = `r round(d, 2)`. These results suggest that there is a small but significant tendency to prefer inherent over extrinsic explanations. 


## Bonus Exercise: Demographics Analysis

### Study 1

```{r}
df.demo <- read_csv('data/tworek2016_study1.csv') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Age, Gender, Excluded) %>% 
  filter(Excluded == 0) %>% # filter out excluded participants
  select(-Excluded) %>% # exclude the excluded variable
glimpse()
```

```{r}
df.demo %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = Age)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 10, color = "black", fill = "lightblue") +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Frequency") +
    ggtitle("Age Distribution") +
    theme_classic()
```

```{r}
df.demo %>%
    tabyl(Gender) %>%
    adorn_totals("row") %>%
    adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1) %>%
    knitr::kable()
```

## Bonus Exercise: Reliability Analysis

### Study 1

```{r}
df.items <- read_csv('data/tworek2016_study1.csv') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(starts_with("ih"), Excluded) %>% # select the 15 items and the Excluded variable
  filter(Excluded == 0) %>% # filter out excluded participants
  select(-ihc1, -ihc2, -Excluded) # exclude the two attention check items and the Excluded variable
glimpse(df.items)
```

```{r}
ih.keys <- list(ih = seq(1, 15)) # no reverse-coded items

# score the items using the scoreItems() function from the psych package
ih <- scoreItems(
  items = df.items,
  keys = ih.keys,
  totals = FALSE)

ih$alpha # Cronbach's alpha
```

### Study 2

```{r}
df.items <- read_csv('data/tworek2016_study2.csv') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(starts_with("ext"), starts_with("ih"), excluded) %>% 
  filter(excluded == 0) %>% # filter out excluded participants
  select(-ihcatch1, -ihcatch2, -ihav, -extav, -excluded) # exclude the two attention check items and the excluded variable
glimpse(df.items)
```

```{r}
ih.keys <- list(ih = c(-seq(1, 15), seq(16, 30))) # no reverse-coded items

# score the items using the scoreItems() function from the psych package
ih <- scoreItems(
  items = df.items,
  keys = ih.keys,
  totals = FALSE)

ih$alpha # Cronbach's alpha
```
